metadata.technology_reasoning: Gravity displacement steam autoclave sterilizers are the most common type used in healthcare and laboratory settings due to their reliability, simplicity, and broad adoption in sterilizing medical instruments and supplies under saturated steam at high pressure.

components.reasoning: The core component where sterilization occurs, typically a robust stainless steel chamber designed to withstand high pressures and temperatures; always a separate, major manufactured assembly.
Provides steam required for sterilization; either integral or separate unit, but distinct in supply chain and essential for operation.
Ensures airtight, pressure-tight seal during cycle; normally procured as a separate assembly including locking mechanisms and gasket.
Controls and monitors sterilization cycles, temperature, pressure, and safety interlocks; typically a distinct electronic module.
Includes steam inlet valves, vacuum valves, drain valves, and pressure relief valves essential for controlling steam flow and sterilization cycles; often modular.
Common in advanced autoclaves to remove air and improve steam penetration; present in gravity displacement models with a vacuum phase.
Critical safety component to prevent overpressure; usually a separate certified valve component.
In autoclaves with electric steam generation, heating elements are primary components distinct from other assemblies.
